name: Ranula

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging diagnosis of ranula

criteria.description: Presence of a painless, translucent swelling in the floor of the mouth
Identification of a cystic lesion arising from the sublingual gland on imaging (ultrasound or MRI)
Histopathological confirmation showing mucous extravasation cyst without epithelial lining

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical swelling plus imaging confirmation of cystic lesion from sublingual gland
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is confirmatory but not always required if clinical and imaging findings are typical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painless translucent swelling in floor of mouth
Bluish cystic lesion under the tongue

common.symptomName: Oral discomfort or foreign body sensation

rare.symptomName: Airway obstruction due to large ranula

laboratory: Usually normal; inflammatory markers elevated if infected
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic lesion in floor of mouth
MRI demonstrating well-defined cystic mass arising from sublingual gland
other: Histopathology showing mucous extravasation cyst without epithelial lining

distinguishingFeatures: Usually smaller, located on lower lip
Not typically in floor of mouth

redFlags: Signs of infection such as fever, erythema, or purulence
references: Neville BW, Damm DD, Allen CM, Chi AC. Oral & Maxillofacial Pathology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2015.
Shafer WG, Hine MK, Levy BM. A Textbook of Oral Pathology. 5th ed. Saunders; 2006.
Regezi JA, Sciubba JJ, Jordan RCK. Oral Pathology: Clinical Pathologic Correlations. 7th ed. Elsevier; 2016.
